svg.title: YouTube Toolkit retrieval routes
svg.desc: A route map of retrieval commands and doctor. Each illustrated command is a colored line connecting the local parts and services it uses, rather than a sequence of execution steps. search uses filter and rank and yt-dlp; with --mode semantic it also reads captions and calls the embedding API (dashed). transcript fetches and archives a transcript, preferring captions; when usable captions are missing and a cloud key is configured, it downloads audio through yt-dlp for cloud speech-to-text (dashed). The README also describes the local STT alternative and the separate stt-setup command. vision uses FFmpeg and OpenCV to pick frames, guided by captions when available, and never invokes speech-to-text. comments fetches and archives one bounded Top sample through yt-dlp, then optionally filters comment text by keyword and interleaves Top and descending like-count order within that sample, returning each match once. metadata and channel share one line to yt-dlp. doctor ends at local readiness checks without network access. Retrieval reaches YouTube through yt-dlp and caption downloads; fresh responses are archived, and a shared trunk carries the retrieval lines to YouTube.

g.text: Retrieval and doctor routes are shown. Dashed lines mark optional paths; services in the shaded zone require network access.
